newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot gas prices rise on cold weather.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot gas prices rise on cold weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natgas prices rose sharply Monday as cold weather blanketed most of North America, market sources said.
Spot prices at Sumas, Wash., the western Canadian export point, were up about 80 cents from Friday in the $3.90-4.10 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range.
Sources attributed the strength to colder weather in the Northwest and Rockies, low inventories in the West and the rally in NYMEX's Henry Hub gas futures.
American Gas Association said last Wednesday that gas stocks in the consuming region West were at 65 percent of capacity as of December 6.
Prices in the Rockies were also up sharply Monday in the $3.10-3.40 per mmBtu range as cold weather struck the region.

At Niagara, the eastern Canadian export point, prices rose by more than 40 cents to about $4.40 per mmBtu following the lead of Henry Hub gas futures and colder weather forecast for the region later in the week.
At AECO storage hub, prices jumped into the C$2.07-2.10 per gigajoule (GJ) range, up nearly 20 cents from Friday.
January prices at AECO were also talked higher in the C$2.17-2.20 per GJ area.

Seasonably cold weather is forecast to remain in Alberta through the end of the week. For Tuesday, forecasters said temperatures in Calgary would be about minus 18 degrees Celsius, or about 10 degrees Fahrenheit.
